name: Hotel Ibex Restaurant
signature_dish: buffet dinner with Bhaga river view
why_it_matters: Hotel Ibex opened the Jispa tourism scene in 1995; the in-house dining hall became the de-facto first proper meal stop after Manali on the Leh-Manali highway. Buffet rotates veg + non-veg, with à-la-carte fallback. Kitchen will pack a lunchbox for the next day's run to Sarchu or Pang.
insider_tip: Buffet runs roughly 8-10am, 1-3pm, 8-10pm — the highway runs to that clock. If you're rolling in late after a Rohtang/Atal-Tunnel delay, message ahead and they'll hold a thali; the kitchen closes hard once last guests are seated.
signature_address: Hotel Ibex, NH-3 Manali-Leh Highway, Jispa, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Padma Lodge Restaurant
signature_dish: buffet with local churpe and butter tea
why_it_matters: Multi-cuisine dining room attached to Padma Lodge — the place travellers tag as the second-best Jispa stop after Ibex. Distinguishing feature is the in-house dairy: local churpe, pure ghee, butter, butter tea, all sourced from the lodge's own animals and Lahauli neighbours.
insider_tip: Breakfast and dinner run as fixed buffets — pre-book by reception in the morning so the kitchen scales properly. Ask for a side of churpe with your butter tea; it's the Lahauli pairing every menu in the valley implies but rarely lists.
signature_address: Padma Lodge, NH-3 Manali-Leh Highway, Jispa, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Gemur Holidays Camp Restaurant
why_it_matters: Tented camp 2km off the Leh highway near Gemur, ranked #1 of 11 Jispa specialty lodgings on Tripadvisor (4.0 / 25 reviews as of 2026). Fixed in-house menu rotates Local, Indian, Chinese, Tibetan and continental — review consensus is 'freshly prepared, hot, and consistent', a low bar most Lahaul kitchens still miss.
insider_tip: Camp is seasonal — typically open mid-May to mid-October. Non-residents can sometimes get a meal if you call ahead, but the kitchen prioritises in-house guests; eat here only if you're staying.
signature_address: Gemur Holidays, near Gemur village, off NH-3, Jispa, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Yak Hotel Jispa Restaurant
signature_dish: thukpa and dal-rice for highway riders
why_it_matters: Roadside hotel-restaurant on the Leh-Manali highway in Jispa, paired with a sister property in Manali. Reviews split — clean rooms and 'well-cooked' food vs 'pathetic and expensive' — but the kitchen does run, which matters when Ibex and Padma are full on a peak August weekend.
insider_tip: There's no in-room service — for tea, food or anything else, walk down to reception. Stick to thukpa, dal-rice and parantha; complex tandoor or Chinese plates are where the negative reviews cluster.
signature_address: Yak Hotel, NH-3 Manali-Leh Highway, Jispa, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Leh Dhaba
why_it_matters: The only Tripadvisor-listed restaurant in this stretch of Lahaul (3.8/5, 8 reviews as of 2026, ranked '#1 of 1 in Jispa'). Sits next to the Darcha check-post — the last named eatery before Baralacha-La and the long blank to Sarchu. Small, cosy, fast service.
insider_tip: Open seasonally with the highway, roughly mid-May to mid-October. Idle for a tea-and-Maggi halt rather than a full meal; the menu narrows on quiet days, and the staff will often suggest what's actually freshly prepped.
signature_address: Leh Dhaba, near Darcha check-post, NH-3 Manali-Leh Highway, Darcha, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Layul Dhaba
why_it_matters: Family-run dhaba in Koksar — the first Lahaul village after Atal Tunnel and the police check-post where every Manali-Leh vehicle pauses. Featured by NDTV's Highway on My Plate; in business since 1975. Mutton curry and kadhi chawal are the two dishes regulars name.
insider_tip: Koksar opens with the highway (typically mid-May to mid-October on the Manali side; the tunnel keeps it accessible later). Order kadhi chawal even if it sounds plain — it's hot, salty and exactly the calorie hit you need before climbing to Keylong/Jispa.
signature_address: Layul Dhaba, Koksar village, near check-post, NH-3, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: White Horizon Homestay Kitchen
why_it_matters: Family kitchen attached to a Homestays-of-India listed property in Gondhla — the village best known for its 8-storey wooden fort. Pure-veg only; menu rotates siddu, thukpa, momos, chowmein and seasonal Lahauli vegetables. The closest you'll get in this stretch to a real home meal as opposed to a hotel buffet.
insider_tip: Meals are paid and on prior notice only — message at least 4-6 hours ahead, ideally morning for an evening sit-down. Non-residents are welcome but not assumed; phrase the request as a booking, not a walk-in.
signature_address: White Horizon Homestay, Gondhla village, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132
